The CEOs of Microsoft, Palo Alto Networks, and Coinbase are all saying the same thing: you do not need the most expensive AI model for most of your work.

Reuters reported this shift on June 29 as a defining trend, and the data backs it up. Roughly 95% of enterprise AI usage still runs on frontier models — the most expensive tier. But routing techniques that assign cheaper open-weight models to routine tasks and reserve frontier models only for complex work can reduce per-token costs by 70 to 90 percent.

That is not a minor savings. For most enterprises, it is a structural cost failure that has been hiding in production since day one.

D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria made the point directly: current growth rates for the big AI providers are the fastest they will ever be. As enterprises learn to route intelligently between model tiers, the revenue concentration at the top compresses.

The takeaway for business leaders is straightforward. AI spending will keep growing — but the share going to premium models will shrink. The companies that build cost-intelligent AI architectures now will have a permanent unit economics advantage over those that do not.
